rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the row's own digit-bearing sweep for its central structuring device undercounts it (five sites claimed, six present), and the mid-verse occurrence at MT 19:21 is the one omitted. OL: the digit holds only under an unstated verse-initial restriction, both pointed runs labelled byte tier re-collate at NFD only, the in-span paseq seg at MT 19:16 is dropped while five setumah are cited, and the postpositive-signature contrast carries no quoted form or verse anchor.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes, object first. The scene-turn formula spliced from MT 19:16's own bytes is “בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא” (skeleton “ביום ההוא”); swept over the staged Masoretic text it stands in SIX verses of the row's own span — MT 19:16, 19:18, 19:19, 19:21, 19:23, 19:24 — against the row's ‘recurs four further times through the row's own span (sweep: 5 sites)’. Five of the six are verse-initial; MT 19:21 carries it mid-verse (skeleton index 38, after “and the Egyptians will know Yahweh”). So the digit is recoverable only under a verse-initial restriction the row never states: the OBJECT is under-specified, not merely the number, and the count also names no unit where campaign practice requires verses or occurrences. TIER CORRECTION to the LF item: the six sites are NOT byte-identical. At byte tier the formula as spelled at MT 19:16 stands in only four verses of chs 19-24 (MT 19:16, 22:8, 23:15, 24:21) and in only ONE verse of ch 19; all six match at accent_stripped and at skeleton. OL's skeleton label is the correct tier and LF's ‘byte-identical’ is a false tier claim inside a challenge. OL's continuation digit reproduces exactly: the same skeleton runs to 13 verses across chs 19-24, adding MT 20:6, 22:8, 22:12, 22:20, 22:25, 23:15, 24:21 — the device structures inside the span and cannot bound it. Both quoted pointed runs re-collate at nfd, not byte, against MT 19:16 and MT 19:24: the NFD-degraded-quote class, real. Marks re-checked against the inventory at MT keys: SAMEKH at MT 19:15, 19:17, 19:18, 19:23, 19:25 — all five correct, correctly typed, correctly held as tier-3 single-witness corroboration and not as a driver; a paseq seg is recorded at MT 19:16 (1 seg) and is undisclosed inside the very span whose parashah marks are all cited, a real symmetry gap. No ketiv/qere note falls in 19:16-25, so the slicing is otherwise safe. OL's last point holds too: the row's contrast with ‘sub-units bracketed by a postpositive divine-speech signature’ names no form and no verse, and the postpositive neum signatures actually available in chs 17-19 are exactly MT 17:3, 17:6, 19:4 (3 verses). The two primaries converge on ONE defect (the count) and OL adds three distinct ones (tier labels, paseq symmetry, unanchored device contrast). None of this moves the boundary: the sixth site sits inside the span and, as both primaries note, argues for the row's unity rather than against it.
rulings.remedy: Author work order, four edits, no boundary change. (1) boundary_rationale: re-splice both pointed runs from the source Masoretic bytes (deterministic author-phase re-splice, never re-keyed and never copied through draft text); test = byte collation returns byte at each cited ref and the Hebrew-normalization dry-run reports no rewrite. (2) boundary_rationale: replace ‘recurs four further times through the row's own span (sweep: 5 sites)’ with a named-object, unit-bearing, tier-labelled count — five verse-initial onsets plus one mid-verse occurrence at MT 19:21, six verses in span at accent_stripped/skeleton tier — and note that the same skeleton continues past the row's close (13 verses across chs 19-24), so the device structures the passage rather than bounding it; test = the sentence names the swept object, the count unit and the tier, and the digit reproduces from the formula spliced out of MT 19:16's bytes. (3) boundary_rationale: anchor the postpositive-signature contrast to a quoted form and a verse ref (the neum signatures at MT 17:3, 17:6, 19:4) or delete the sentence; test = every device contrast in the row carries a quoted form and a verse anchor. (4) device_notes and boundary_evidence_refs: disclose the paseq seg at MT 19:16 (1 seg, single-witness, count-only, no intra-verse position) alongside the five setumah citations; test = the span-relevant seg-disclosure symmetry sweep over 19:16-25 finds nothing undisclosed.

rulings.challenge_claim: The 'no internal tier-1 seam' warrant is argued past its strongest counterevidence — a verse-initial divine-speech onset at MT 20:3 coinciding with the row's only in-span parashah mark — the frame at MT 20:2 is mislabelled as interpretive when it introduces the command, and both pointed runs labelled byte tier re-collate at NFD only.
rulings.grounds: All three strands verify from bytes. MT 20:3 opens verse-initially with “וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה”, and the amar/vayomer-plus-YHWH adjacency census lists that verse among its MT keys — a tier-1 speech-frame signal under the evidence policy whatever weight it is finally given. The row nonetheless asserts flatly that ‘the bytes offer no internal tier-1 seam’ between command and interpretation, without quoting or answering that onset: the assertion is stated, not tested. The mislabel is byte-confirmed. MT 20:2 carries “בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָה֮ בְּיַ֣ד יְשַׁעְיָ֣הוּ” followed IN THE SAME VERSE by the imperative run “לֵ֗ךְ וּפִתַּחְתָּ֤ הַשַּׂק֙” and the compliance clause “וַיַּ֣עַשׂ כֵּ֔ן” — that is the COMMAND frame; the interpretation of the sign-act (‘as my servant Isaiah has walked …’) opens at MT 20:3 under the divine-speech onset. Calling MT 20:2 the interpretive frame inverts the two, and the inversion sits in the row's load-bearing sentence. Both quoted runs re-collate at nfd, not byte, against MT 20:2 and MT 20:3: the NFD class. Marks re-checked at MT keys: SAMEKH at MT 19:25, 20:2, 20:6, all correct and correctly typed; the mark at MT 20:2 is disclosed as mid-span but never set against the tier-1 onset it abuts, and the tier-3 layer is correctly not asked to drive anything. Credits confirmed: the servant handling is right — the my-servant form at MT 20:3 is a NAMED referent (the prophet), correctly kept apart from the unnamed servant-figure zones, and the row decides no referent question; the operative-category deviation from the report label toward continuous third-person narration is honestly disclosed rather than argued away. OL asks for engagement, not for a cut, and I decide no construal here either.
rulings.remedy: Author work order, three edits, no boundary change. (1) boundary_rationale: re-splice both pointed runs from source bytes; test = byte collation returns byte at oshb:Isa.20.2 and oshb:Isa.20.3 and the Hebrew-normalization dry-run reports no rewrite. (2) boundary_rationale: re-cut the frame description so MT 20:2 is named as the command frame (time-frame plus messenger clause, imperative run, compliance clause) and MT 20:3 as the divine-speech onset opening the interpretation; test = each frame named in the row matches that verse's own bytes in function, checked against the spliced runs. (3) boundary_rationale: replace the bare 'no internal tier-1 seam' assertion with an argued treatment of the verse-initial divine-speech onset at MT 20:3 — state why the sign-act's own narrative frame holds across it — keeping the setumah at MT 20:2 as tier-3 single-witness corroboration only and never as the reason; test = the row's strongest internal counterevidence is quoted and answered rather than left unstated. A split at 20:2|20:3 is a respan PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption and is not proposed here.

rulings.challenge_claim: The sentence that defeats the row's own rival is falsified by the row's own quoted bytes — MT 21:6 carries a divine-speech frame with an explicit addressee, and the span's petuchah stands immediately before it; two in-span paseq segs go undisclosed and both pointed runs re-collate at NFD only.
rulings.grounds: The core strand is decisive and self-inflicted. The row's rejected alternative says the banquet-to-commissioning transition 'is not marked by an addressee or frame-device shift in the bytes', two sentences after the row itself quotes “כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֵלַ֖י אֲדֹנָ֑י” from MT 21:6. Both halves of that sentence fail. Frame-device: the divine-speech census lists MT 21:6 among the divine-frame sites and names it explicitly as a non-adjacent title form — a koh-amar frame unquestionably stands at the very transition called unmarked. Addressee: beyond the first-person dative “אֵלַ֖י” inside the formula, the surrounding bytes carry an actual shift — MT 21:5 addresses a plural group (“ק֥וּמוּ הַשָּׂרִ֖ים”) while MT 21:6 directs the speech to the prophet and commands him singly (“לֵ֚ךְ הַעֲמֵ֣ד”). The rival the row concedes is therefore left undefeated by the row's own quoted material. Corroboration re-checked at MT keys: the mark at MT 21:5 is a PE, correctly typed as the rarer type against the 41 PE / 168 SAMEKH inventory over 209 marked verses, with SAMEKH at MT 20:6 and MT 21:10 — all accurate, all correctly held at tier-3 single-witness and never as a driver, and it sits at the 21:5|21:6 junction. Paseq segs are recorded at MT 21:2 (2 segs) and MT 21:8 (1 seg) and neither is disclosed although both parashah marks in the span are — a real symmetry gap. Both pointed runs re-collate at nfd against MT 21:1 and MT 21:6: the NFD class. Credits confirmed: the massa header at MT 21:1 is genuinely verse-initial; the frame ownership at MT 21:6 is correctly named as divine despite the intervening dative, which is the harder half to get right; the continuation-fold disclosure on the header verse is accurate in the staged layout and correctly held at tier-4. OL also observes that the same frame class is given seam force ten verses later; that is adjudicated on the row where it is charged. This ruling adjudicates the defective sentence only — the 21:1-10 watchman-vision construal is a known low-confidence hold and is NOT decided here.
rulings.remedy: Author work order, four edits, no boundary change. (1) boundary_rationale: re-splice both pointed runs from source bytes; test = byte collation returns byte at oshb:Isa.21.1 and oshb:Isa.21.6, Hebrew-normalization dry-run clean. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: re-cut the concession so it states what actually stands at MT 21:6 — a divine koh-amar frame carrying a first-person dative, with the address changing from MT 21:5's plural imperatives to a singular command to the prophet — and then gives the ground on which the vision is nonetheless held whole across it; test = no sentence in the row is contradicted by a run the row itself quotes, and the rival is answered rather than restated. (3) device_notes: disclose the paseq segs at MT 21:2 (2 segs) and MT 21:8 (1 seg), single-witness, count-only, no intra-verse position; test = the span-relevant seg-disclosure symmetry sweep over 21:1-10 finds nothing undisclosed. (4) Because strongest_rejected_alternative is a driver-dependent field, re-open observed_substrate_signals, unit_type and confidence alongside the re-cut and re-check each against the corrected warrant; test = the dependent fields are re-derived, not carried over. Any split at 21:5|21:6 is a respan PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption; the held construal stays held.

rulings.challenge_claim: The bounds are byte-clean and survive challenge, but both pointed runs labelled byte tier re-collate at NFD only and the 'bracket' reading overstates an intra-verse doubling whose two members differ in the bytes; no byte-true device straddles either seam because the preceding unit's watch vocabulary is a different root.
rulings.grounds: The two charged defects are real; the reviewer's own cross-seam clearance is not, and the corrected finding adds a third defect. (a) NFD confirmed: both pointed runs re-collate at nfd, not byte, against MT 21:11. (b) The doubling confirmed: member A “שֹׁמֵר֙ מַה מִלַּ֔יְלָה” and member B “שֹׁמֵ֖ר מַה מִלֵּֽיל” fail identity at byte, at accent_stripped AND at skeleton — the night-forms differ (skeleton “מלילה” against “מליל”), so no tier makes the two members identical; only the watchman member itself repeats, and only at skeleton tier. The row's 'carries a repeated watchman question as its own bracket' is thus an untiered recurrence claim that is false as identity at every tier, and 'bracket' is the wrong figure besides: the repetition is immediate and intra-verse, not an inclusio around the two-verse unit, and the refrain-keyed substrate signal rides on that reading. (c) CORRECTED FINDING, new: OL clears cross-seam cohesion on the ground that the preceding unit's watch vocabulary is 'a DIFFERENT root — … and “כָּל” at MT 21:8'. That is byte-false at MT 21:8. “כָּל” is a shamar-root noun — its skeleton “כל” contains “שמר” contiguously — and the shamar skeleton stands at exactly MT 21:8, 21:11 and 21:12 in ch 21, so the root DOES straddle this row's opening seam. Only the watcher-noun at MT 21:6 and the lookout-noun at MT 21:8 are the genuinely different tsaphah root. The continuity is skeleton-tier and therefore weak, not the byte-true device the cohesion rule aims at, and the seam is not threatened — verse-initial massa headers stand at MT 21:11 and MT 21:13, tier-1, and the bounds hold — but the row owes the disclosure and the reviewer cleared it in error. Marks re-checked at MT keys: SAMEKH at MT 21:10 and MT 21:12, correct and correctly typed; no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note falls in 21:11-12, so nothing further is owed there. Severity stays low: no strand touches the boundary.
rulings.remedy: Author work order, three edits, no boundary change. (1) boundary_rationale: re-splice both pointed runs from source bytes; test = byte collation returns byte at oshb:Isa.21.11, Hebrew-normalization dry-run clean. (2) boundary_rationale: replace 'carries a repeated watchman question as its own bracket' with a tier-labelled description — an immediate intra-verse doubling whose watchman member repeats at skeleton tier while the night-forms differ at every tier — and re-check the refrain-keyed substrate signal against the corrected reading, demoting it if the corrected description no longer supports a refrain; test = every recurrence claim in the row names its tier and reproduces at that tier from the spliced bytes. (3) device_notes: disclose the shamar-root continuity across the row's opening seam (skeleton tier: MT 21:8 into MT 21:11-12) together with the tier-1 header warrant that survives it; test = the cross-seam cohesion sweep over both of the row's own seams finds nothing undisclosed, and the disclosure names its tier.

rulings.challenge_claim: An undisclosed catchword hooks this row's closing verse to the next unit's at an oracle join, the mark prose places a setumah inside a span it does not fall in, the in-span paseq is dropped at the very verse whose setumah is cited, and the header run re-collates at NFD only.
rulings.grounds: Three strands verify exactly; the fourth is overstated and its tier is under-named. (a) MARK POSITION, confirmed: the row's span is Isa.21.13-Isa.21.15 and its device_notes say 'a setumah opens this row at Isa.21.12'. The inventory records SAMEKH at MT 21:12 — closing the verse BEFORE the span. The mark is real and correctly typed; its stated position relative to the row is false. The neighbouring row in the same part uses the correct form ('a setumah precedes this row at Isa.21.15'), so this is a local slip rather than a convention. (b) PASEQ, confirmed: a paseq seg is recorded at MT 21:15 (1 seg) and is undisclosed in the very verse the row cites for its setumah — one verse, two seg layers, one engaged and one dropped. (c) NFD, confirmed: the header run re-collates at nfd against MT 21:13; it is the row's only pointed run. (d) OVERSTATED and MIS-TIERED: the catchword is real but weaker than charged. “קֶ֣שֶׁת” at MT 21:15 and “קֶ֛שֶׁת” at MT 21:17 differ ONLY in accent, so they match at accent_stripped, not merely at skeleton as the challenge says — and nothing here is byte-true. It is an ordinary common noun (skeleton sweep: 8 verses book-wide, 3 verses in chs 20-23 — MT 21:15, 21:17, 22:3); it does not straddle the row's own seam directly, since it skips the seam verse MT 21:16; and both sites sit inside the same massa-header-bound Arabia material, where lexical continuity is expected rather than probative. Disclosure is still owed under the cross-seam cohesion rule, but the corrected finding is a weak accent_stripped-tier lexical hook, NOT 'the byte support' for the rival the row concedes. Credits confirmed: the massa header at MT 21:13 is genuinely verse-initial and correctly claimed. This ruling does not decide the Arabia-oracle construal, which is a known hold.
rulings.remedy: Author work order, four edits, no boundary change. (1) device_notes: correct the mark position — the setumah at MT 21:12 PRECEDES this row's span rather than opening it; test = every mark-position word in the row matches that mark's actual verse relative to the row's own span, and the span-relevant mark-disclosure symmetry sweep passes. (2) device_notes: disclose the paseq seg at MT 21:15 (1 seg, single-witness, count-only, no intra-verse position) alongside that verse's setumah; test = no verse cited for one seg layer leaves another seg layer in the same verse undisclosed. (3) boundary_rationale: re-splice the header run from source bytes; test = byte collation returns byte at oshb:Isa.21.13, Hebrew-normalization dry-run clean. (4) device_notes: disclose the bow-noun recurrence at MT 21:15 / MT 21:17 with its tier NAMED as accent_stripped (skeleton sweep: 3 verses in chs 20-23) and state that the seam warrant is the divine-speech onset at MT 21:16, which survives it; test = the disclosure names the tier and the count unit, and the seam warrant is restated in terms that survive the disclosed continuity.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the row treats a mid-oracle divine-frame formula as sufficient to open a fresh row while the neighbouring row in the same part treats the same device-class occurrence as carrying no cutting force, and the row does not reconcile the two even though its own rationale names the parallel. OL: the parallel is false at every tier — the two openings differ in token order — and it collapses the adjacent/non-adjacent title distinction on which the earlier site's classification rests.
rulings.grounds: Both items land on one sentence — 'paralleling the identical frame construction opening the wilderness-of-the-sea vision report earlier in this part' — and they are DISTINCT defects, not one; the second does not dissolve the first. OL's is byte-decisive: MT 21:6 opens “כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֵלַ֖י אֲדֹנָ֑י” and MT 21:16 opens “כִּי כֹ֛ה אָמַ֥ר אֲדֹנָ֖י אֵלָ֑י” — the dative precedes the title at the first site and follows it at the second. The two fail identity at byte, at accent_stripped AND at skeleton (“כי כה אמר אלי אדני” against “כי כה אמר אדני אלי”). 'Identical frame construction' is therefore false at every available tier, and it additionally carries no tier label where campaign practice requires the tier named at write time. The distinction OL protects is load-bearing: the divine-speech census names MT 21:6 explicitly among the non-adjacent title forms whose divine ownership must be ARGUED rather than read off an adjacency, while MT 21:16 is the plain adjacent form that needs no such argument — flattening them erases the ground on which the earlier frame was owned. LF's is a warrant defect and SURVIVES OL's finding: the census lists both MT 21:6 and MT 21:16 under divine frames and neither under royal-messenger, so the two sites are one device CLASS even though they are not one form, and the row gives that class seam force here while the neighbouring row holds its own occurrence internal to an unbroken unit on the stated ground that no 'addressee or frame-device shift' marks it. Neither row reconciles the opposite weights, and this row's disclosed alternative addresses only whether to keep the Arabia oracle whole. Both pointed runs re-collate at nfd against MT 21:16 and MT 21:17: the NFD class. The bare unpointed root mention beside the remnant quote is a skeleton-grade mention carrying no tier label. Marks re-checked at MT keys: SAMEKH at MT 21:15 and MT 21:17, correct and correctly typed. Credit confirmed: the remnant object is named correctly as the shear NOUN, kept apart from the Shear-Jashub name and from the reactivating clauses — exactly the four-way discipline this book demands. The defect is warrant quality, not boundary falsity: MT 21:16 does carry a divine koh-amar frame, and the preceding row is plain scene description.
rulings.remedy: Author work order, three edits; WARRANT repair only. (1) boundary_rationale: re-splice both pointed runs from source bytes and tier-label the bare unpointed root mention as skeleton-grade; test = byte collation returns byte at oshb:Isa.21.16 and oshb:Isa.21.17, Hebrew-normalization dry-run clean, and no untiered Hebrew mention remains in the row. (2) boundary_rationale: replace 'the identical frame construction' with the byte-true relation — the same divine koh-amar frame CLASS but not the same form: the two differ in token order and fail identity at byte, accent_stripped and skeleton, and MT 21:6 is the non-adjacent title form while MT 21:16 is the adjacent one; test = the corrected sentence reproduces from the two spliced runs at the tier it names AND preserves rather than erases the adjacency distinction on which the earlier site's divine ownership rests. (3) boundary_rationale or strongest_rejected_alternative: state the reconciliation — why this one device class carries seam force at MT 21:16 and none at MT 21:6 — or withdraw the parallel outright; test = the test that killed the original, namely that the same device class is not assigned opposite seam weights inside one part without a stated ground, checked against the neighbouring vision-report row's own warrant. Any consequent respan of either row is a PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption; the 21:1-10 and 21:13-17 construals are held and are not decided here.

rulings.challenge_claim: Both: the row's stated warrant for stopping at Isa.22.11 rests on the claim that the in-that-day frame opening the next unit is 'not present anywhere in this row's own span', and that claim is falsified by MT 22:8 inside the span. OL adds that the formula is verse-initial at neither seam-side site, that it runs through the seam and beyond as cross-seam cohesion evidence, and that the paseq segs are cited under a WEB prefix although the seg layer is Masoretic.
rulings.grounds: The shared core is confirmed and it is the row's load-bearing sentence. MT 22:8 carries the day-formula “בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא” against the run the row quotes from MT 22:12, “בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא” — so the frame the row calls absent from its own span stands inside it, and the seam is argued on a false discriminator. The two items are the SAME defect, differently framed and differently tiered. TIER CORRECTION to the LF item: the two runs are NOT byte-identical. They differ in exactly one codepoint — the accent borne by the second token, etnachta at MT 22:12 against zaqef qatan at MT 22:8 — so they match at accent_stripped and at skeleton and fail at byte. OL's tier is exact; LF's 'collates byte-identical' is a false tier claim inside a challenge. LF's English citation is verbatim against the staged WEB text at web:Isa.22.8. OL's added findings verify: the formula is verse-initial at NEITHER site (it follows the verb of looking at MT 22:8 and the divine subject at MT 22:12, skeleton indices 23 and 22), so an onset-versus-adjunct restriction — which the row does not make — would not separate them; and the skeleton runs THROUGH the seam and past it at MT 22:8, 22:12, 22:20 and 22:25 (4 verses in ch 22), making it cross-seam cohesion arguing continuity rather than the discriminating force claimed for it, undisclosed as such. What survives at 22:11|22:12 is the other ground the row also states — “וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת” introduces a grammatical subject absent from 22:1-11 — so the seam may well hold; the defect is the warrant, not necessarily the boundary. Credits confirmed and worth recording: every pointed run in this row reaches BYTE tier on re-collation (MT 22:1, MT 22:5, MT 22:12), the one row in this cluster free of the NFD class; the paseq counts are right at 1 seg each for MT 22:2 and MT 22:11 and correctly given as bare counts without intra-verse position; NO parashah mark falls in 22:1-11 and the row correctly leaves that absence unclaimed rather than treating it as counterevidence; the verse-initial header claim at MT 22:1 is right; and poetry_lines is 0 across all eleven verses in the staged layout, accurate and correctly held at tier-4. OL's witness point also stands: those paseq segs are cited under a web: prefix although the seg layer is keyed to the Masoretic witness alone — ch 22 is identity-numbered so the digits land, but the attribution does not. High severity is right: this is a load-bearing sentence contradicted by the row's own span.
rulings.remedy: Author work order, three edits plus dependent-field re-open; no boundary change. (1) boundary_rationale: strike or re-cut the sentence claiming the in-that-day frame is 'not present anywhere in this row's own span' — MT 22:8 carries it — and re-argue the closing seam on the ground that survives, the fresh grammatical subject in the divine-summons clause opening MT 22:12; test = the test that killed the original, namely that no sentence in the row asserts the absence of a form standing inside the row's own span, and the surviving warrant is stated independently of the day-formula. (2) device_notes: disclose the day-formula as CROSS-SEAM cohesion — accent_stripped/skeleton tier at MT 22:8, 22:12, 22:20 and 22:25 (4 verses in ch 22), verse-initial at neither seam-side site — and state the warrant that survives it; test = a device the row's span shares with the following unit is disclosed as continuity evidence BEFORE any discriminating force is claimed for it. (3) device_notes: re-prefix the paseq citations to the Masoretic witness (oshb:Isa.22.2, oshb:Isa.22.11), keeping the single-witness, count-only, no-position form; test = every seg-layer claim is cited under the witness that carries the layer. (4) Driver re-cut re-opens its dependent fields: re-derive observed_substrate_signals, strongest_rejected_alternative, unit_type and confidence against the corrected warrant; test = the dependent fields are re-derived rather than carried over. The 22:11|22:12 seam itself is not decided here; any respan is a PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption.

rulings.challenge_claim: The closing formula is not a bracket in the bytes — a byte-identical divine-speech run straddles the row's own closing seam into MT 22:15 — the stacked-title recurrence is claimed without its tier, and the petuchah and paseq are cited under a WEB prefix although both seg layers are Masoretic.
rulings.grounds: All three strands verify from bytes. CROSS-SEAM: the run spliced from the close of MT 22:14, “אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה”, collates at BYTE tier against MT 22:15, where the following unit opens with the koh-amar divine frame — the census lists MT 22:15 among the divine-frame sites. The run the row treats as unit-CLOSING immediately re-opens as the next unit's frame element: byte-true cohesion straddling the row's own closing seam, undisclosed, which under the cross-seam cohesion rule argues continuity against the row until disclosed and answered. The asymmetry OL names is real and internal to this cluster: the preceding row DID disclose and reason about the stacked-title recurrence across this row's OPENING seam, arguing that the repetition marks a new sub-unit opening rather than binding across; nothing equivalent is offered at the closing seam, and the closing case is the stronger of the two because the shared run reaches byte tier rather than skeleton. BRACKET TIER: the stacked title spliced from MT 22:12, “אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת”, and from MT 22:14, “אֲדֹנָ֥י”, fail identity at byte AND at accent_stripped — the accents differ on all three tokens and the final token at MT 22:14 carries a meteg, which the accent_stripped tier retains — matching only at skeleton (“אדני יהוה צבאות”). So 'the same stacked divine title' is a skeleton-tier recurrence stated as if unqualified, where the tier must be named at write time. WITNESS: the petuchah and paseq are cited as web:Isa.22.14 and web:Isa.22.13 although both seg layers are keyed to the Masoretic witness alone. Credits confirmed: every pointed run in the row reaches byte tier on re-collation; the PE at MT 22:14 is correctly typed and not conflated with SAMEKH; the paseq at MT 22:13 is correctly counted at 2 segs and correctly presented as a bare count with no intra-verse position, which is the only sourceable form of that claim.
